abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
          <jats:sec>
            <jats:title>Key message</jats:title>
            <jats:p>The GWAS and testing with <jats:italic>Yr</jats:italic> gene linked markers identified 109 loci including 40 novel loci for all-stage and adult plant stage resistance to stripe rust in 459 US contemporary hard winter wheat genotypes.</jats:p>
          </jats:sec>
          <jats:sec>
            <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
            <jats:p>Stripe rust is a destructive wheat disease, caused by <jats:italic>Puccinia striiformis</jats:italic> f. sp. <jats:italic>tritici</jats:italic> (<jats:italic>Pst</jats:italic>). To identify sources of stripe rust resistance in US contemporary hard winter wheat, a panel of 459 Great Plains wheat genotypes was evaluated at the seedling stage against five US <jats:italic>Pst</jats:italic> races and at the adult plant stage in field environments in Oklahoma, Kansas, and Washington. The results showed that 7–14% of the genotypes were resistant to <jats:italic>Pst</jats:italic> races at the seedling stage, whereas 32–78% of genotypes were resistant at the adult plant stage across field environments, indicating the presence of adult plant resistance. Sixteen genotypes displayed a broad spectrum of resistance to all five <jats:italic>Pst</jats:italic> races and across all field environments. The panel was further genotyped using 9858 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) generated from multiplex restriction amplicon sequencing (MRASeq) and the functional DNA markers linked to the known stripe rust resistance (<jats:italic>Yr</jats:italic>) genes <jats:italic>Yr5</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>Yr15</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>Yr17</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>Yr18</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>Yr29</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>Yr36</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>Yr40</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>Yr46</jats:italic>, and <jats:italic>QYr.tamu-2B</jats:italic>. A genome-wide association study (GWAS) was performed using genotypic and phenotypic data, which identified 110 SNPs and the functional markers linked to <jats:italic>Yr15</jats:italic> and <jats:italic>Yr17</jats:italic> to be significantly associated with stripe rust response. In addition, <jats:italic>Yr5</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>Yr15</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>Yr17</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>Yr18</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>Yr29</jats:italic>, and <jats:italic>QYr.tamu-2B</jats:italic> were detected by their functional DNA markers in the panel. This study identified 40 novel loci associated with stripe rust resistance in genomic regions not previously characterized by known <jats:italic>Yr</jats:italic> genes. These findings offer significant opportunities to diversify and enhance stripe rust resistance in hard winter wheat.</jats:p>
          </jats:sec>
title: Genome-wide association mapping for the identification of stripe rust resistance loci in US hard winter wheat
